answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent reviewers confirm fraud. A trellis of reputation links can raise the required bond for newcomers, while a pigment-like marker records which stake backed each claim. Splitting one operator into many identities then multiplies the capital at risk; the attacker must fund every bond and lose them on detected abuse. The delta is that extra identities no longer come cheaply.
